scope: K4: construction reservations and completion into funded recruit eligibility, attraction, population/cost, acceptance, and downstream aftermath.

Unbuilt plan/debt lifecycle, destruction reset, built furniture/storage and debt settlement.

evidence_anchors.symbol: Immigrant requirement variants and recruitment metadata
Attraction occupancy/value and missing population/spawn checks

findings.claim: Construction adds a typed unbuilt plan and debt. When buildable and funded, Collective creates a Task::construction with the plan CostInfo, takes the resource, and associates task ID with the plan. Removing an unbuilt plan cancels its task and returns that cost.

Completion tracks built furniture and storage positions, claims nearby squares, and recalculates population increase using completed furniture counts, with a fenced-animal count for relevant furniture. Max population is configured capacity plus built-furniture increase plus INCREASE_POPULATION creatures; ordinary population size excludes NO_LIMIT creatures.

Immigrant offers are periodically weighted candidate generation; unmet requirements may reduce candidate probability, but acceptance rechecks strict eligibility. Attraction counts built furniture/items, subtracts already claimed attraction slots, and requirements scale with group size. The offer also needs population room unless NO_LIMIT and enough valid spawn positions; the population check blocks when current population is already at or above max, and this check does not test whether the full group would exceed remaining capacity.

Eligibility supports technology, sunlight, resource balances, required built furniture, turn/pregnancy/tutorial/unlock, attraction, and ally recruitment. CostInfo checks full group cost; ExponentialCost increases based on currently extant recruits after a free allowance.

RecruitmentInfo filters known matching enemy collectives to unstunned matching creatures, keeping their configured minimum population. Acceptance transfers an existing recruit into the player collective; ordinary offers add their generated creatures, while a RecruitmentInfo offer falls back to its generated candidate only if no existing recruit is found at mutation time. Successful acceptance occupies required resources/attractions, tracks members, consumes or regenerates the offer, and emits a join message. UI caller exposes accept/reject/auto behavior.

Completed facilities act as both attraction stock and population ceiling inputs, while an accepted minion can reserve attraction value. This suggests a space/means/choice loop; this is a code-derived design inference, not measured balance or proof about current commercial releases.

No construction task is assigned without funds/buildability. An unbuilt plan cancellation returns task completion cost and removes plan/debt. An immigration accept with missing requirements or too few spawn squares exits without adding a creature.

fingerprints.symbol: finite resident jobs and owned stock

verified_support: Site-project phases compile to current simulation commands, claims, and world facts; no separate construction scheduler.

Preview checks actor/participant availability and simultaneous site-job capacity. Timed jobs reserve site slots, freeze costs/effects, then release on completion, cancellation, or lost support; refunds follow explicit command policy.

Society currently creates an authored finite resident roster at explicit meeting, with separate accounts/inventories and two one-job-at-a-time work sites. Nested local-life jobs use actual resident stock and credits.
Work plans store IDs/revisions and accepted-job receipts, not a second job engine.

Recruitment and independent actor spawning already exist elsewhere in YAIR: a paid field commission can spawn the fieldSurveyor before its project finishes. The gap is not generic recruitment infrastructure.
current_yair_inspection.actual_missing_consumer: A site capacity currently limits simultaneous jobs only. Completing a site project writes a fact/receipt but does not add durable resident occupancy capacity for a completed facility or an explicit funded Invite/Decline consumer whose acceptance claims that occupancy. Existing YAIR actor spawning and paid commissions exist; the missing join is completed facility -> durable resident occupancy -> funded invitation choice and occupancy aftermath.
current_yair_inspection.caveat: Requested src/js paths resolve to repository-root src/*.js here. The worktree has existing dirty/untracked project changes; only the designated JSON note was written by this lane.

one_original_proposal.name: One funded guest-room invitation
one_original_proposal.action_and_choice: Finish one small original guest-room project, inspect one available local helper’s terms, and choose Invite or Decline. Invitation is explicit and one-time; building alone does not grant a person.
one_original_proposal.prerequisites: Completed room; one open durable resident slot; available willing helper with an authored role; player at supported local contact. Recheck at acceptance.
one_original_proposal.proposed_cost: Pay/reserve actual owned construction materials through current item costs. On acceptance transfer a stated fixed amount of existing player coins to the resident and one real starter kit if their role requires it. Specific numbers/items remain proposals; no duplicated funds or stock.
one_original_proposal.capacity: One slot is granted only when the room is complete. This differs from the existing site capacity, which only limits concurrent jobs. Refusal consumes no slot. Define room closure/destruction while occupied before implementation.
one_original_proposal.aftermath: The invited helper gets a stable independent person/actor identity, finite owned means, and one authored opt-in job/service using the current scheduler; agreement/results appear only after observed actions. Decline changes neither inventory nor helper means. Do not add passive upkeep until food/housing consequences are authored.
one_original_proposal.actual_missing_consumer: No durable completed-room-to-resident-occupancy projection or funded Invite/Decline consumer currently joins facility completion to a capacity-claiming resident invitation. YAIR already has actor spawning and paid commissions, so this proposal adds only that missing occupancy/choice join.
one_original_proposal.save_decision: Durable identity, occupancy and role/job state need an explicit schema migration or compatibility decision plus save/reload verification before playable delivery.
one_original_proposal.later_playable_acceptance: Show actual material construction; slot only after completion; full/unfunded/unsupported invite unavailable; truthful accept and decline receipts; accepted resident uses actual funds/stock in useful work; room teardown has a defined rule; save/reload preserves identity/slot/balances. This lane ran no builds or playtests.
